deck.q: A ripe banana.
The inside of a lime.
A London bus.
Miles Davis, 1959. Kind of what?
The Baron who flew the Fokker triplane.
Dorothy follows a road of this brick.
Beethoven never wrote one, but Gershwin did — a Rhapsody in what?
The house the American president lives in.
deck.why: It is white — which is not on this board. Take the closest thing to no colour at all and argue about it.

deck.q: What a jealous person is said to be with envy.
The colour of a bruise on its second day.
deck.why: Then it goes yellow, and you have missed.

deck.q: Sinatra's eyes.
The flag of surrender, near enough.
deck.why: White again. Nearest thing on the board wins the argument.

deck.q: A cowardly person's streak.
Robin Hood's forest and his tights.
The colour of the sky at the very top on a clear day.
deck.why: Straight up is darker than the horizon. Look sometime.

deck.q: A traffic light telling you to think about it.
deck.why: Amber, if you are being formal.

deck.q: Prince's rain.
deck.why: Purple Rain — and purple is violet's louder cousin.

deck.q: What a novice belt is in most martial arts.
deck.why: White. Again. This board has a gap and everybody knows it.

deck.q: The colour you go when you hold your breath too long.
A pillar box, a phone box, and a guardsman's coat.
The sea, according to every crayon ever handed to a child.
deck.why: It is grey. Say blue anyway.

deck.q: Old money for a ten-shilling note.
deck.why: It was brown. Nobody said these were fair.

The fruit that gave a county in Ireland its nickname and a
king his house.
deck.why: The clue is doing a lot of work.

deck.q: What the Beatles' submarine was.
Rust, on a night bus, under a sodium lamp.
deck.why: Sodium light kills red. Everything under it goes orange.

deck.q: The Orison's own front door.
deck.why: It has been repainted four times and it is still green underneath.
